sources.beginner: nextgen-panel: bs-burial-heat-explorer (panels/basin/BurialHeatExplorer.jsx:121-130) opens on the capstone case (shale, 2000 m, 1000 m burial) and prints all six to 6-8 dp; all six are also closed-form hand-calcs taught in m02-m04; every value is printed verbatim in the capstone walkthrough lesson
sources.intermediate: nextgen-panel: bs-kinetics-explorer (panels/basin/KineticsExplorer.jsx:124-130) opens at rate 3, 100 degC, Type II and prints all six to 8 dp (rate 1 is one click); anchors are closed forms; every value is printed verbatim in the capstone walkthrough lesson
sources.advanced: nextgen-panel: bs-charge-explorer (panels/basin/ChargeExplorer.jsx:118-123) opens on the 600 m reference run with the no-erosion twin and prints all six (Ro/TR 8 dp, T 6 dp, masses 3 dp); every value is printed verbatim in the capstone walkthrough lesson

fields.recommendation: Lesson text prints every graded answer to full precision (the capstone walkthrough lesson lists all six values and tolerances, and the values recur in several other lessons), and the course panel opens on the capstone case by default. Recommend the owner decide whether to (a) strip graded values from lessons, keeping the method and a different worked case, and (b) move the capstone to a case the panel does not preload (a different depth, rate, temperature or erosion amount the learner must enter). Tolerance and display need no change.
fields.evidence: Tile "Solid thickness in 100 m at surface" fmt(read.solid100, 8); fmt = v.toFixed(d) (BurialHeatExplorer.jsx:18). Lithology defaults to shale (line 23). Closed-form grain integral is also taught (beginner m02/l04), so a hand-calc is possible. Printed resolution 1e-08 is far inside tol 0.05.
